references.text: Lot meets two angels at the city gate of Sodom and bows to the ground, parallel to Abraham's meeting with the three men
Jacob lifts his eyes, sees Esau coming, and bows to the ground – similar language to Abraham's reaction
The angel of the Lord appears in human form to Manoah and his wife, another example of a divine visitation
Joshua meets the commander of the Lord's army and falls to the ground – a divine figure appearing in human form
Encourages hospitality, for some have unknowingly entertained angels as guests – a direct allusion to Abraham's hospitality
Parallel in the immediate response to divine presence: running to meet them and throwing themselves down in submission.
Deep parallel: Revelation of divine presence leading to immediate submission (bowing with face to the ground).
Thematic connection regarding God's presence at the entrance of the tent: hidden in human form (Gen) versus revealed as a pillar (4 Mos).
